assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ordered mesoporous silica (MCM-41 and successors) opened a new class of crystalline-like, template-designed porous solids with tunable pore size beyond zeolites, enabling catalysis, adsorption, drug carriers and hard-templated carbons. It is a clear case of designed architecture giving new function, and it reshaped how porous-materials chemists think about liquid-crystal templating.
assessment.attribution: Mobil's Kresge and Beck made the decisive MCM-41 discovery; Stucky and Zhao (SBA-15, cooperative assembly, large-pore robust silicas) and Ryoo (MCM-48 extensions, ordered mesoporous carbon) plus Inagaki (FSM-16/organosilica) are all strong claimants. A three-person configuration forces hard choices; I lean to the Mobil discovery plus the mechanistic and large-pore generalization by Stucky.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of independent confirmation; pore-wall structure is amorphous but the mesostructure is rigorously established by XRD, TEM and sorption. Recognition is fully mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority between Mobil and the independent Japanese FSM-16 work is disputed in the literature.
Whether Zhao or Ryoo should displace Stucky or Beck in a three-person prize is unresolved.
Walls are amorphous, so some may regard it as less fundamental than crystalline framework chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cell efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in about a decade, and the materials have spawned LEDs, detectors and a large body of defect and structure-property chemistry. Few recent chemistry discoveries have had comparable breadth, and the structure-function story is rich.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park the solid-state 2012 efficiency step, Snaith the mesosuperstructured and planar architectures that proved the materials work as true absorbers. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel are also major but I judge the three named to be the cleanest chain of credit; the list is crowded and any trio will exclude deserving people.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency records are repeatedly reproduced worldwide, but long-term operational stability, lead toxicity and scale-up remain unsettled. Prize timing may be somewhat early for commercial impact but the scientific impact is established.
uncertainties: Operational stability and commercial viability are unproven.
Overlap with Grätzel's dye-sensitized solar cell recognition complicates configuration.
Attribution among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Seok and Kanatzidis is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Iijima's 1991 high-resolution electron microscopy identification of multiwalled nanotubes, and the 1993 single-wall tubes from Iijima and Bethune, created a whole field of low-dimensional carbon. The atomic structure was established directly by TEM and diffraction, which for me is exactly the sort of structural evidence that makes a discovery convincing. Impact on materials, electronics and composites is large.
assessment.attribution: Iijima is the central figure. Bethune's independent single-wall synthesis was reported back-to-back in 1993. Endo produced earlier vapor-grown carbon fibers with hollow tubular cores, which makes priority arguments real. Fullerenes already received a prize, but this is a distinct discovery.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of confirmation, with chirality-resolved structure and properties well characterized. Applications are slower than early hype, but scientific recognition is long mature.
uncertainties: Priority claims for earlier hollow carbon filaments (Endo and others) are disputed.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or physics.
Commercial impact has lagged expectations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new pharmacological modality, converting binding into catalytic removal of proteins, with clinical candidates advancing. Chemically it is an original and conceptually clean idea with growing impact on drug discovery and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies produced the original PROTAC concept and demonstration; Handa and colleagues identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, explaining glue degraders; Ciulli, Gray and others extended it with VHL ligands and degrader design. The credit chain is plausible but the field is large and crowded, so allocation is not settled.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing, with many clinical trials, but no PROTAC drug is yet approved, and long-term clinical validation is incomplete. Likely slightly premature compared with older candidates.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet.
Credit split between PROTAC inventors and the thalidomide/cereblon glue-degrader line.
Roles of Ciulli, Gray and Kim in a three-person configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers made it possible to determine structures from micro- and nanocrystals before radiation damage, and to follow reactions in time. This is an enabling structural method that lets a whole community see what it could not, in the same spirit as electron crystallography for nanocrystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof-of-principle with Fromme on photosystem I nanocrystals and a large collaborative team; Schlichting contributed to time-resolved serial crystallography and mechanistic applications; Hajdu helped to conceive the idea. The collaborative nature of the first experiments makes a clean three-person attribution hard.
assessment.maturity: Method is established across multiple XFEL facilities and extended to synchrotron serial methods, but facility access is limited and the number of fully new mechanistic results remains moderate relative to its promise. The picture is still evolving.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Chapman, Fromme, Hajdu, Schlichting and others (e.g. Neutze, Spence) outside the supplied credit.
Competition with cryo-EM and microED for similar problems.
Number of decisive chemical insights is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts maximize metal utilization and link molecular and heterogeneous catalysis, with potentially tunable and uniform active sites. They have drawn enormous attention and the conceptual framing is attractive.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Fe1/FeOx work by Qiao, Wang, Liu, Zhang and coworkers introduced the term and clear demonstration; Datye and Li contributed key characterization and theory. Earlier single-atom observations by others complicate priority. Three-person credit would be defensible but not clean.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is wide but evidence quality varies; many claimed single-atom structures rest on aberration-corrected STEM and XAS that sample little of the material, and the true nature of active sites under reaction conditions is often debated. Probably premature for a prize.
uncertainties: Structural proof of isolated sites under operando conditions is frequently weak.
Priority relative to earlier atomically dispersed catalysts.
Industrial impact still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors, which chemically convert one base to another without double-strand cleavage, are a genuinely chemical approach to genome editing, with fast clinical translation. The underlying idea was original, and the impact on biomedical research is large and growing.
assessment.attribution: Liu's group built both cytosine (Komor) and adenine (Gaudelli) base editors; Nishida and Kondo independently reported related cytidine-deaminase fusion editing. Liu is the clear leader, so a one-person or Liu plus trainees configuration is unusual; the supplied credit supports a three-name proposal only if the committee accepts trainee recognition.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials and patient treatment have begun, which supports timeliness, but the broader genome-editing area already received the 2020 prize and committee may see this as a follow-up better saved for later or paired with prime editing.
uncertainties: Overlap with prime editing (B035) and CRISPR 2020 prize.
Whether trainees should share recognition.
Long-term safety and off-target data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The dye-sensitized nanocrystalline solar cell combined a high-surface-area mesoporous TiO2 film with molecular dyes and a redox electrolyte, an elegant architecture-driven function. It launched a field of molecular photovoltaics and opened the path to perovskite cells.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 Nature paper by O'Regan and Grätzel is the central work; Hagfeldt contributed later device and mechanism work. Grätzel's centrality is clear; O'Regan's inclusion is defensible as first author.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with many independent confirmations, and recognized by other major prizes. However commercial impact has been modest, and the overlap with the perovskite candidate could make awarding both awkward.
uncertainties: Commercial impact limited compared with silicon and perovskites.
Overlap with candidate B016 and Grätzel's credit in both.
Timeliness: the field has declined as perovskites rose.
